response: {"proposal_name":"Magnetoceptive Sense (Geomagnetic Field Sensing)","physical_basis":"Detection of static and quasi-static magnetic fields (primarily Earth's geomagnetic field, ~25-65 microtesla) via specialized biological transducers such as magnetite-based mechanoreceptors or radical-pair photochemical reactions in cryptochrome-like molecules. Unlike vision, this does not depend on absorbing propagating electromagnetic radiation (photons) but on the alignment/torque response of magnetically susceptible particles or spin-state chemistry to a persistent field vector.","information_content":"Absolute directional heading relative to magnetic north (compass bearing), field inclination angle (which correlates with latitude), and local field intensity anomalies (useful for detecting magnetic mineral deposits, metallic objects, or geomagnetic disturbances). This information is vectorial and geophysical rather than pertaining to light intensity, sound frequency, chemical identity, or body configuration.","functional_role":"Enables absolute orientation and long-distance navigation independent of vision, sound, or memorized landmarks; supports functioning in darkness, underground, underwater, or in featureless terrain; allows true north/south determination and geographic self-localization (via inclination) even with no external reference cues; also enables detection of hidden ferromagnetic or magnetically anomalous objects (e.g., metal detection at a distance).","justification":"This modality is physically and informationally distinct from all eight existing senses. It differs from Visual because it responds to static/slowly varying magnetic fields rather than oscillating EM radiation in the 300-1000nm band, and the transduction mechanism (mechanical torque on magnetite crystals or quantum radical-pair spin dynamics) is fundamentally different from photopigment isomerization. It differs from Vestibular because vestibular sensors detect inertial acceleration and rotation of the head relative to gravity and motion, not alignment with an external planetary magnetic field; a stationary, non-accelerating body still has a magnetic heading, but has no vestibular signal to report it. It is not chemical (Olfactory/Gustatory) since no molecules are being sensed. It is not somatosensory (Tactile/Proprioceptive) since no mechanical deformation of skin, joints, or muscles is involved. And it is not Interoceptive since it conveys information about the external environment's geophysical structure, not internal physiological state. The resulting capability—absolute geomagnetic orientation and navigation without any of the existing seven external/internal senses—cannot be synthesized post hoc by combining outputs of the other eight modalities, making it a genuinely novel sensory addition."}
prompt:
You are participating in a scientific study on AI creativity and conceptual innovation.

BACKGROUND:
We have defined a sensory system with 8 modalities. Each modality is specified below by its physical basis (what it detects), information content (what data it provides), and functional role (what it enables):

| # | Modality        | Physical basis                                                              | Information content                                              | Functional role                        |
|---|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| 1 | Visual           | Electromagnetic radiation, 300-1000 nm (UV, visible, near-infrared)          | Light, color, brightness, and spatial pattern information          | Scene and object recognition            |
| 2 | Auditory         | Mechanical pressure waves, 1 Hz-100 kHz                                      | Sound, pitch, volume, and acoustic pattern information              | Sound source localization               |
| 3 | Tactile          | Mechanical vibrations and pressure, 5-800 Hz on skin surface                 | Touch, texture, vibration, and contact information                  | Surface texture and pressure sensing    |
| 4 | Olfactory        | Airborne chemical molecules across ten scent categories                     | Categorical scent/chemical identity information                     | Substance identification                |
| 5 | Gustatory        | Dissolved chemical molecules across five taste categories                   | Taste-category information (sweet/sour/salty/bitter/umami)          | Ingestion guidance                      |
| 6 | Proprioceptive   | Joint angles and muscle tensions via muscle/tendon/joint mechanoreceptors    | Body configuration and movement information without visual input    | Body-state estimation                   |
| 7 | Vestibular       | Linear acceleration and angular velocity via inner-ear semicircular canals   | Head position, motion, and orientation information                  | Balance and motion detection            |
| 8 | Interoceptive    | Internal physiological signals (heart rate, respiration, skin conductance, temperature, hunger, thirst, fatigue, pain) | Homeostatic and internal-state information | Homeostatic regulation |

YOUR TASK:
Propose a NINTH sensory modality that would be genuinely novel - not just a refinement or combination of existing ones. Your proposal should include:

1. Modality Name: Clear, descriptive name
2. Physical Basis: What physical phenomenon it detects
3. Information Content: What specific information it provides
4. Functional Role: What capabilities it enables
5. Justification: Why this is genuinely novel (not reducible to existing modalities)

Be creative but rigorous.

Provide your response in the following JSON format:
{
  "proposal_name": "Name of the ninth modality",
  "physical_basis": "Description of physical detection mechanism",
  "information_content": "Description of information provided",
  "functional_role": "Description of enabled capabilities",
  "justification": "Explanation of why this is genuinely novel"
}
